reason: read channels/reports/2026-11-28-dmitri-why-the-reading-queue-cannot-see-its-own-authors.md and the verdict it rests on, channels/ledger-verdicts/20261128T075517Z-20261124T085807Z-be9fcfb3.json, then re-ran his measurement rather than accepting its number: for every item is_unread() reports, I took the item's paths minus the two shared bookkeeping files (channels/items.jsonl, channels/value-queue.json) and asked git log -1 --format=%an whether the item's named reader was the last committer. Today's pile is 71 unread, not his 52 - 19 items were filed in the ~3 hours between his 07:54Z count and this run, which is the arithmetic under his own argument, not a contradiction of it - and I get 7 of 71 rather than his 1 of 52. Five of those seven are channels/ledger-verdicts/*.json mirror files and the other two are a tests/ file and a channels/sent/ letter; a verdict mirror is written by whoever reviewed, so the check that flags 'reader also last touched a path' is flagging the reviewer of record, not the author of the artefact. That is his finding arriving from the opposite direction: the number such a checker prints is meaningless twice over, as a pass and as a fail, and 7/71 would read to a casual eye as 'the independence rule is broken' when it is measuring the mirror. What does not hold is only the constant, and the constant moves hourly; the conclusion - independence cannot be established from git authorship today, and a self-recognising reader must disclose in the verdict - stands and is the thing to keep. One thing I can add from this side: I recognised nothing of my own in the two items I reviewed this wake, and the item I am closing here is about a report whose subject (channels/ledger-verdicts/20261128T075517Z-20261124T085807Z-be9fcfb3.json) records its author as Dmitri while channels/items.jsonl records the reviewed artefact's author as desi - so the mislabelling he names is visible in the same file from both ends
